# CI Adoption Notes

Adopt generated CI and release automation on GitHub and Codeberg.

## Generator Contract

Simit owns its generated workflow files and marks them with:

```text
# Generated by simit. Manual edits will be reported as ci=drift.
```

The first non-check `simit init ci` run saves effective CI options to the
existing `simit.toml` or Cargo metadata, creating `simit.toml` only for projects
without config. Flake config must declare its strategy explicitly when enabling
release-plz; Simit does not create a second config source. Check for drift:

```sh
simit init ci --platform <forgejo|github> --check --diff
```

Until CI options are saved, drift errors print the full regeneration command,
including the effective runtime, runner, workspace, and optional gates.

Generated steps that invoke Simit (such as the `flake-wiring` check and Windows
packager's `cargo install`) pin the generating revision or version. A Nix build
embeds its clean flake `self.rev`
(`git+https://github.com/caniko/simit.git?rev=<sha>`,
`cargo install --locked --git … --rev <sha> simit`). Cargo and dirty-tree builds
lack a source revision and pin the crate's release tag instead
(`?ref=refs/tags/<version>`, `cargo install --locked simit --version =<version>`).
Regenerating with a different Simit therefore moves the pin and reports drift.

Example saved CI settings:

```toml
[ci]
platform = "forgejo"
runtime = "nix"
runner = "atlas"
workspace = true
with_deny = true
with_audit = true
with_docs = true
with_msrv = true
```

## Native Cargo on Crow

Crow uses the same Rust image as Actions unless `[ci.crow].image` overrides it.
Native Crow checks use `--locked`, so commit `Cargo.lock` before enabling them.

```toml
[ci]
provider = "crow"
platform = "forgejo"
runtime = "cargo"
workspace = true
workspace_strategy = "aggregate"     # one .crow/build.yaml
exclude_packages = ["test-fixtures"]
package_features = { app = ["sqlite"] }
all_features = false
unit_tests_only = true
clippy_all_targets = false
format_all_rust_files = true
format_excludes = ["vendor/**"]

[ci.crow]
combine_steps = true
cargo_home = ".crow-cargo"
build_jobs = 4
strip_ci_debug = true
shallow_clone = true
paths_include = ["**/*.rs", "**/Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock", "simit.toml", ".crow/**"]
paths_exclude = ["docs/**"]
```

Aggregate CI excludes the listed members. `package_features` applies only when
`all_features = false`, and then only to selected members on the first test and
Clippy pass. Unit-only checks split library and binary-only crates as needed.
`clippy_all_targets = false` skips integration tests, benches and examples.
On Crow and Actions, `format_all_rust_files` checks every tracked `.rs` file
against the workspace edition, including `include!()` files. `format_excludes`
takes Git pathspecs.

`combine_steps` runs setup, formatting, Clippy and tests in one container, then
runs optional checks. It conflicts with custom check commands and per-step
runners. `cargo_home` defaults to `/tmp/.cargo`; use a workspace-relative path
to share registry downloads across containers. `strip_ci_debug` disables
incremental builds and debug info for dev and test profiles. `build_jobs` caps
compilation parallelism. Explicit `[ci].extra_env` values win. `shallow_clone`
skips LFS and fetches one commit; do not combine it with `skip_clone` or
history-dependent checks. Path filters apply to push and PR triggers.

For compiler caching, put `sccache` on the runner image's `PATH` and set
`[ci.crow.sccache].enabled = true`. Configure the backend with `env` and use
`secret` for a same-named Crow secret. PR checks use the cache too; never give
untrusted PRs privileged cache credentials.

Crow renders each `[[ci.manual_gates]]` entry as `.crow/manual-<id>.yaml`.
Set `runtime = "nix"` or `"cargo"` to override the main workflow runtime, `env`
for gate variables, and `secret` for a same-named Crow secret available only to
that gate. Run `simit init ci --ci-provider crow --check --diff` to verify drift.

Track quota usage with `simit ci usage --repo crow:owner/repo --since 7d
--budget-minutes 2500`. The report shows measured wall-clock minutes and a linear
30-day projection; add `--json` for the structured `budget` object.

## Local gate

For projects without hosted CI, `local_gate = true` under `[ci]` generates
`scripts/ci-local.sh`. It replays every eligible generated Actions `ci*.yaml`
`run` step or Crow build and CI command in CI order, without replaying runner
environment variables or secrets, and skipping manual gates and hosted-only
steps (such as `$GITHUB_*`, Actions expressions or global Git configuration).
It then builds each `[ci].nix_builds` installable within the `[ci.nix_build]`
job limits.

Put local-only checks, such as a development browser suite, in
`[ci].local_gate_steps`. Each entry runs under its own name after the derived
steps and Nix builds, and appears in `--list` and `SIMIT_LOCAL_ONLY` matching:

```toml
[ci]
local_gate = true
local_gate_steps = [
  { name = "Browser suite", run = "CI=1 nix develop -c npm --prefix tests/browser run test:ci" },
]
```

Use unique, non-empty, single-line names and non-empty `run` values. This key
requires `local_gate = true`. Step changes report drift until `simit init ci`
regenerates the script.

```sh
bash scripts/ci-local.sh --list                  # list steps
SIMIT_LOCAL_ONLY="clippy|test" bash scripts/ci-local.sh  # run matching steps
```

The generated marker lets `simit init ci --check` report hand edits as drift.
Set `local_gate` to false to retire the script.

## Primary package

Wherever Simit needs one package to represent a workspace (such as the README
crates.io badge and name, description, license and homepage fallbacks for AUR,
COPR, APT, Scoop, Chocolatey and release setup), it defaults to the
alphabetically first workspace member. Adding a crate to a virtual workspace
can change the default. Pin it with a top-level key before any table:

```toml
primary_package = "bekiper-annotate"

[ci]
# ...
```

An explicit `--package` wins. A name that is not a workspace member is an error.

## Release-plz on GitHub Actions

Newly enabling Rust publication on a supported GitHub Actions project selects
`release-plz` by default. Existing publishers keep their implicit or explicit
`members` / `coordinated` policy until you migrate:

```sh
simit init ci --platform github --publish-crates --publish-strategy release-plz
# For a Cargo workspace, also pass --workspace.
simit init ci --check --diff
```

Set `--publish-strategy members|coordinated|release-plz` to choose explicitly.
The older `--coordinated-publish[=false]` still maps to coordinated/members;
Simit rejects conflicts and saves even an explicit legacy default (`members`).
Release-plz requires crate publication (`--publish-crates` or the matching
setting), even with binary artifacts. Artifact-only generation keeps the legacy
strategy.

Release-plz computes versions and per-package changelogs and coordinates
crates.io publication and signed tags. Separate credentialed Simit workers
deliver the prepared release PR data and verified crate archives. Simit owns
configured binary builds, checksums, attestations and hosted assets; in that
case `release-plz.toml` sets `git_release_enable = false` so only Simit creates
the hosted release. Release-plz creates it for crate-only projects. Single-crate
tags honor `[release].tag_prefix`; multi-crate tags are `<package>/v<version>`.
Release via the PR, not `simit release` or manual bumping/tagging.

`init ci --check` and registry auditing cover all three generated files:
`release-plz.toml`, `.simit/release-plz.py`, and
`.github/workflows/release-plz.yaml`. Migration retires generator-owned
member/coordinated publishers. Before generation, reconcile any hand-written
competing publishers or release-plz config at the paths Simit reports.
Migration follows literal local scripts and reusable workflows, honoring
workflow/job/step working directories and custom shell templates. Reconcile
missing, external or opaque local files, local actions and remote reusable
workflows explicitly. Calls to `cargo publish`, `cargo release`, `cargo-release`
and `release-plz` count as competing publishers.
Simit scans tracked and unignored local scripts regardless of extension, not
ignored untracked build outputs. A generated marker alone cannot exempt a
publisher that migration leaves active.
The scan consumes environment assignments and supported wrapper options before
inspecting executables; it does not silently skip opaque options (such as
directory changes or split-string execution), variable-expanded executables or
shell `eval`, requiring explicit reconciliation instead (use literal names so
the scan can see retained publishers). Simit inspects the `actions-rs/cargo`
command input and requires reconciliation for unresolved command expressions. In explicit Python, Node, Ruby and PowerShell
steps, it inspects literal local executables in known native launch calls,
including multiline argv lists, but treats data arguments as data.
Reconcile native execution overrides such as Python's `executable=`, Python/Node
`cwd` and Ruby `chdir`. Direct `env` shebangs consume supported options and
assignments before selecting the interpreter; computed or unsupported forms
fail closed.
Simit uses Bash syntax trees to inspect, without evaluating, literal commands
in nested command/backtick and process substitutions, including in assignment
values, parameter expansions and data arguments. Reconcile malformed
substitutions. Single-quoted text does not execute.
This scan is bounded, not a general program analyzer. Review generated
executables, computed/downloaded commands and remote reusable workflows before
enabling publication.

Initial support covers Cargo and Nix, a single publishable crate with binary
releases, and ordinary multi-crate Cargo workspaces. Explicit release-plz
selection rejects package selectors, alternate registries, mixed-language
monorepos, other CI providers, and workspaces with multiple publishable crates
and repository-wide binary releases. Unsupported new setups keep the existing
publishing default.

### Automation credentials and signing

Configure these repository secrets before enabling default-branch execution:

| Name                          | Purpose                                                                                |
| ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN`           | Repository-scoped PAT with contents and pull-requests write access                     |
| `CRATES_IO_API_TOKEN`         | crates.io publication token                                                            |
| `RELEASE_PLZ_GPG_PRIVATE_KEY` | Armored OpenPGP private key authorized by the committed `[release.signing].trust_root` |
| `RELEASE_PLZ_GPG_PASSPHRASE`  | Optional signing-key passphrase                                                        |

Set the repository variable `SIMIT_PUBLISHER_REVISION` to an independently
qualified immutable Simit revision that supports release-plz archive admission.
Qualify and update any engine enrolled for the older tag publishers before
adopting release-plz.

A repository-installed GitHub App is preferred over a PAT. If using an App, set
a repository App ID variable and private-key secret, then configure:

```toml
[ci]
publish_crates = true
publish_strategy = "release-plz"

[ci.release_plz]
app_id_variable = "RELEASE_PLZ_APP_ID"
app_private_key_secret = "RELEASE_PLZ_APP_PRIVATE_KEY"
# Optional secret-name overrides:
registry_token_secret = "CRATES_IO_API_TOKEN"
signing_key_secret = "RELEASE_PLZ_GPG_PRIVATE_KEY"
signing_passphrase_secret = "RELEASE_PLZ_GPG_PASSPHRASE"
```

Workflow generation and `release secrets contract --json` validate App pairs
and credential names identically. Incomplete pairs never fall back to a PAT
contract.

Place these tables under `package.metadata.simit` or `workspace.metadata.simit`
if Cargo metadata holds the config. Without an App, `token_secret` overrides
the PAT secret name. The generated App token grants only contents/pull-requests
write access to this repository. The default `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot trigger
release-PR CI or downstream tag workflows; it serves only read-only selection
and update preparation. Release-plz's temporary repositories inherit
repository-scoped Git authentication. See the
[upstream token contract](https://release-plz.dev/docs/github/token).

`simit release secrets contract --platform github` includes the release-plz
secret/variable requirements. `simit release verify` uses that contract for all
required credentials, including custom registry secrets and crate-only releases,
without requesting an unused default registry secret. The workflow checks credentials before writes, derives its Git identity from
the authorized key's UID, enables `tag.gpgSign` and probes signing. It deletes
private key material afterward. Downstream signed-tag/trust-root admission
still applies. This integration uses an explicit crates.io token; do not assume
existing trusted-publishing registration covers the new workflow.

### Revision qualification and recovery

Simit pins the CLI to release-plz **0.3.172** (reviewed source
`8b523fa6c4eb4992f18365ac50a196b4dc6a1013`). The fixed Linux worker verifies the
upstream GNU binary's SHA-256 before execution, independent of project MSRV.
Credential-free Nix jobs prepare updates through `nix develop -c`; credentialed
jobs use the verified standalone binary and data-only operations. Actions use
the shared immutable registry. The generated config sets `release_always = false`:
ordinary default-branch pushes update a release PR; merging it starts
publication.

Release-plz may publish the last commit of a merged release PR, not the event's
branch tip. Simit requires a generated release branch in the same repository
and a matching head/body receipt. It verifies the original head's OpenPGP
signature against the event's committed trust root and resolves the immutable
revision, fetching squashed PR heads absent from the checkout with the
read-only token. Merge commits select the PR head; squash merges select the
squash commit. A credential-free job runs project checks and required gates on
the selected revision and verifies archives with modern Cargo's
unpublished-workspace dependency staging.
Selection scans the complete native push range for exact PR merge commits
introduced by that push, so later commits cannot hide a release merge or
replace its revision. Multiple release PRs in one push or
incomplete/non-fast-forward history require reconciliation before publication or
PR preparation can advance. Publication rechecks selection, and a Cargo wrapper
rejects uploads from any other revision. Qualifying branch HEAD alone is
insufficient.

The publication worker independently rebuilds every archive from the selected
Git tree via the qualified engine's data-only Cargo path. Project Cargo config,
wrappers, hooks, Nix expressions and build scripts never run with release
credentials. The release-plz Cargo adapter uses the same archive verifier and
registry transport for uploads and rejects build-capable commands.
Before any release-plz upload or tag push, Simit reconciles every existing
workspace version, even crates release-plz skips. Each upload repeats the check.
Published archives must match their registry checksums and qualified contents.
Unchanged members may differ only in an older ancestral Git SHA. Changed
contents, dirty/non-ancestral source bindings, wrong identities and yanked
versions halt the entire release.

Preparation runs `release-plz update` and its available semver checks without
release credentials. A fresh worker indexes only regular-file changes to
`Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` and `CHANGELOG.md`, then signs and delivers the tree.
The worker protects an existing PR with an exact-head lease and refuses to
overwrite manual edits. Close or explicitly reconcile upstream-created release
PRs before the first generated update. The pushed signed commit binds the
prepared summary and exact prior PR body. Failed PR creation/update API calls
can resume without repushing; an already-delivered response is a no-op. Recovery
checks the committed trust root, exact event parent and admitted tree and never
discards unrecognized/manual changes.
Superseded events never create or update a PR, even on retry. A current-source
successor can replace an interrupted older signed update only if its exact
prior-body binding still matches and its single source parent is ancestral to
the current event. It delivers newly admitted current-source data, not the
stale tree. Failed publication also blocks the next PR update until reconciled.

Each immutable push runs separately, without in-progress cancellation. GitHub's
native `queue: max` admission group excludes queue waits from the selection
job's 360-minute execution timeout. Once admitted, Simit waits up to 350 minutes
for the preceding default-branch run via the read-only Actions API. The
predecessor must already have completed selection, so its admission wait does
not count.
[GitHub queues up to 100 pending jobs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/control-workflow-concurrency#example-queueing-multiple-pending-runs);
overflow is canceled, and FIFO follows queue arrival, not event/run-number order.
Out-of-order admission fails rather than deadlocking the occupied slot.

Before selection, the gate reads predecessor job outcomes newest first on the
default branch. Only publication is irreversible.

- Successful `publish` ends the walk: nothing older can be pending. An
  overall-successful run that skipped publication is not a stopping point.
- Failed, canceled or timed-out `publish`, or unidentifiable jobs, block until
  retry or reconciliation: crates or tags may be half-published.
- A selected but unpublished release blocks, typically after
  `release-plz-qualify` fails on a merged version bump. The successor's own push
  range would omit that version.
- Continue past predecessors that examined their range, selected no release,
  and published nothing. Their delivery failures cannot hide an older
  unresolved publication.
- A predecessor that failed at the predecessor gate (`Require the preceding
release-plz event to succeed` failed and `Resolve release-plz immutable
revision` is exactly `skipped`) never examined its push range. The successor
  extends its own selection back to the last event that did complete a
  selection, and the publish recheck receives the same base, so a release merge
  in that gap is qualified and published now. A missing, renamed, failed,
  cancelled or successful selection step is not proof of an unexamined range and
  keeps blocking. A run whose `skipped` conclusion means no job ran is treated
  like an unexamined range. If no earlier event bounds that range, the gate
  fails closed instead of advancing.

A successor's signed-head guard resumes or rejects a half-delivered release PR.
Simit retries paginated GitHub API reads but fails closed on incomplete
provider history. Actionlint 1.7.12 lacks `queue` support; Simit's Nix
development/test environments use `nix/actionlint-queue.patch` to validate
`single|max` and reject `max` with literal `cancel-in-progress: true` without
suppressing other checks. Downstream lint needs equivalent support until upstream
adds it.
Release PR delivery skips superseded default-branch revisions; publication
never cancels mid-run. Release-plz uploads crates **before** pushing tags and
skips published versions on retry. A failed tag push can therefore leave a
published crate untagged; rerunning may not repair the tag. Before recovery, inspect the failed
run, selected SHA and crates.io package contents. An authorized maintainer
must create and verify the missing signed tag at that exact SHA, then push
with credentials that trigger binary workflows. Never move a published release
tag or republish different contents under the same version.

Simit's own Cargo metadata explicitly adopts this strategy. Live qualification
requires the automation token/App and authorized signing key to be provisioned.
Before downstream rollout, retain evidence of release-PR CI, the intended
revision's crates.io publication, a verified signed tag, and its binary release.

## Generic CI vs Release Publishing

### Execution ownership and duplicate work

Repository formatting, full-flake validation, dependency audit and policy, and
declared integration gates run once in the first selected member's workflow.
Each member keeps its tests, Clippy, documentation, MSRV and package checks.
One CI owner runs a project-wide `check_command` or Omnix replacement; each
per-package release workflow keeps its independent publication prerequisites.
Update required contexts on migration and keep the shared gate required.

Rust/Nix CI runs `nix flake check --no-build` for
`components = ["flake-evaluation"]`. Selecting `"checks"` runs full validation
without repeating evaluation if both are set. The independent lane's all-system
evaluation and Python's evaluation plus selected builds remain separate because
their scopes differ. An evaluation-only migration requires complete replacement
build coverage, not just successful selected builds.

Nextest replaces the ordinary test harness but keeps a separate Cargo doctest
pass for doctest-enabled library targets in each feature mode. It omits
doctests for binary-only packages and `unit_tests_only`. `unit_tests_only`
selects library tests, or binary unit tests when selected packages have no
library target; aggregate CI considers all selected members. Across Actions,
split-runner and Crow layouts, Omnix replacement drops generic Cargo tests and
Clippy, while augmentation keeps both.

To qualify PRs and validate default-branch pushes once per source, explicitly
set the repository's real default branch in the relevant policies:

```toml
[ci]
push_branches = ["trunk"]

[ci.nix_build]
push_branches = ["trunk"]
```

These are trigger filters, not successful job-level skips. Empty lists keep all
push branches. The primary filter supports GitHub Actions Rust/Python/flake and
monorepo qualification CI; the matrix filter supports GitHub Actions matrices,
including grouped builds. If you require independent push/PR originals, keep
`separate_events` until custody enrollment and required contexts migrate
together. Simit rejects branch filters with explicit `separate_events` before
generation. Release/tag triggers keep their separate policy.
`[prebuild].push_branches` filters the native prebuild's branch pushes the same
way; pull requests still run it and releases still reuse it via `workflow_call`.
The reusable `release: true` entry requires `[release.github]` or
`[prebuild].release_archives`. With no caller, publish-only prebuilds omit it,
its tag/changelog/keyring validation and `attic_token` indirection. They read
the Attic token from the repository secret.
Simit-generated Crow `build` and `ci` workflows run on all pull requests, but
only on pushes to `${CI_REPO_DEFAULT_BRANCH}` or default updater refs
(`simit/update/**`). PR pipelines gate other branches without repeating work on
metered agents.
A flake-only project (no `Cargo.toml` or `pyproject.toml`) with
`provider = "crow"` gets `.crow/ci.yaml`: `nix flake check --no-build`, then
one `nix build --no-update-lock-file` step per `[ci].nix_builds` installable
(a full `nix flake check` when the list is empty or `components` lists `checks`), on the `[ci].runner` agent.
The clone keeps full history but sets `lfs: false`: Nix reads Git objects,
not LFS content. Crow rejects Actions-only options such as `extra_setup`,
`[ci.cache]` or `[ci.nix_build]` tuning.
Projects without a GitHub mirror set `[prebuild].provider = "crow"`. Then
`simit init ci --prebuild-only` renders `.crow/prebuild.yaml` with the
`[ci.crow]` image and labels. It always clones and builds prebuild installables
only on pushes to `${CI_REPO_DEFAULT_BRANCH}`. With `publish_attic`, it runs
`attic_app` and exports the `[release.attic].token_secret` Crow secret as
`ATTIC_TOKEN` for harbor-rs `mkAtticPush`. It requires `[prebuild].nix_builds`;
`[ci].nix_builds` stays with PR qualification. A Crow primary, which does not
qualify `[ci].nix_builds`, must list those installables only in
`[prebuild].nix_builds`. The Crow prebuild provider rejects release archives,
GitHub runner labels and branch filters. Switching providers removes the other
generated prebuild.

The publishing prebuild never runs on PRs. To add separate secret-free PR
qualification, optionally set `[prebuild].qualify` to a list of installables,
usually flake checks. Those workflows use the same image and labels on pull
requests and default-branch pushes: `.crow/prebuild-qualify-flake-check` runs
`nix flake check --no-build`; one `.crow/prebuild-qualify-<name>` builds each
`qualify` and prebuild `nix_builds` installable, named by final attribute.
Workflows run in parallel, each with the repository timeout, and never update
the lock file. Remove `qualify` to retire them, or opt into bounded, serialized
qualification:

```toml
[prebuild]
provider = "crow"
nix_builds = [".#packages.x86_64-linux.server"]
qualify = [".#checks.x86_64-linux.clippy"]
qualify_serial = true
qualify_max_jobs = 1
qualify_cores = 2
qualify_timeout_minutes = 90
qualify_capture_results = true
# Optional: release the evaluator before realizing frozen derivations.
qualify_split_evaluation = true
```

`qualify_serial` chains whole workflows, not just steps. Positive job/core
limits apply to all qualification commands; timeout sends TERM, then KILL after
30 seconds. Result capture logs the checkout commit, lock-file SHA-256, exact
installable, exit status, flake metadata and Nix's JSON derivation/output map,
even on failed builds. It rejects dirty tracked source and propagates Git
inspection errors. Clone and qualification containers don't share tools, so
Git LFS bootstrap initializes the local clean filter using `git-lfs` from the
flake's pinned `nixpkgs` before checking the smudged checkout. Bootstrap uses
the same job/core/timeout limits. Fresh receipt directories prevent stale
results on early failure.
Result capture logs read-only cgroup-v2 memory snapshots before work and on
exit: membership, selected path, byte limits/current/peak, swap limits/current
and `memory.events`/`memory.events.local`. Missing counters log as unavailable
without changing the qualification exit status. A labeled mount-root fallback
may include other workloads; don't attribute its counters to this step.
Compare before/after OOM counters: a nonzero count or cumulative peak alone
doesn't prove a new OOM. Container death may prevent the exit trap and final
snapshot. Capture never changes or resets limits or counters.
`qualify_split_evaluation` requires result capture. It records the
`build --dry-run --json` plan, then realizes only those derivations and output
names in a separate process (`--stdin`), without reevaluating the flake
installable. It keeps the plan with the final JSON result even on failure and
never builds after planning fails. It accepts static derivation installables
and explicit outputs but fails closed on opaque store paths or dynamic
derivations. Indirect GC roots protect derivations while the evidence directory
exists; result links root outputs. Workers must allow per-user GC root writes
under `${NIX_STATE_DIR:-/nix/var/nix}`. Timeout/job/core limits and
qualification gates are unchanged. Splitting can reduce evaluation/build memory
overlap but doesn't raise memory limits or guarantee a build fits.
These are **log receipts**, not Actions artifacts. Configure and verify the
Crow repository timeout and log retention separately before enabling a release
gate (for example, at least 90 minutes and 14 days). For off-server evidence
or recovery, download logs and keep referenced output closures. Repository
policy and cached realization don't prove fresh test execution.
Distinct MSRV, feature, platform, extracted-package, all-system evaluation and
fresh-execution checks are separate acceptance cases, not duplicate work.

### Simit's own CI ownership

Simit uses evaluation-only primary CI with these required execution owners:

| Coverage                                                                                                                          | Owner                       |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| Formatting, flake evaluation, all-feature and no-default-feature tests/Clippy, Rustdoc, generator drift, package inventory        | `test`                      |
| Production package build and its filtered-source all-feature tests; dependency closure                                            | `qualify`                   |
| Locked advisory audit, dependency policy, filtered custody assets, public-package cache policy                                    | `qualify`                   |
| Complete production-generator regeneration and retained source/tree/binary/workflow evidence, including signed-release publishing | `qualify`                   |
| All workflow lint, including both signed-release publishers                                                                       | `qualify-release-generator` |

Full-flake outputs remain available locally. CI doesn't rebuild their
formatting, Clippy, test or Rustdoc equivalents before native validation. It
still builds and tests the source-filtered production package separately.
Rustdoc's shell carries Rust dependencies and mdBook; site builds own Plinth.
Push and PR originals remain explicitly enrolled for custody. Native-platform,
transport, observer-isolation and publisher-boundary qualifications keep their
own workflows and required contexts. Both replacement qualifiers cover all
primary CI push branches, even without an open PR. Newer revisions supersede
older runs within, not across, push and PR concurrency groups.

### Native grouped Nix executor

Grouped workflows invoke `simit ci nix-group`. Before adopting regenerated
workflows, set repository variable `SIMIT_CI_ENGINE_REVISION` to the exact
40-character lowercase Git revision of a qualified Simit engine that includes
that command. Provisioning builds `github:caniko/simit/<revision>#default`
(never the producer checkout) and records the selected source revision and
executable SHA-256 in the evidence root. Missing or malformed enrollment, or an
engine lacking the command, fails the job with no moving-ref or Python fallback.
Runs without repository variables (such as fork pull requests) fail enrollment
unless `[ci.nix_build].engine_revision` commits the same exact revision as a
fallback: the workflow then uses
`vars.SIMIT_CI_ENGINE_REVISION || '<revision>'` (so an enrolled variable still
wins) and keys the engine cache by that effective revision. Because a
`pull_request` run already executes its head's workflow file, the committed
fallback grants forks no extra authority. This read-only bootstrap is not
enrollment for privileged completion custody or release publishing, which use
separate authority contracts.

Producer `extra_env` bindings apply only after provisioning (setup, validation,
execution, and diagnostics). Provisioning clears shell startup files, applies
controlled Nix configuration with public substitution, clears Nix
`access-tokens` for its build (including tokens from a preceding Nix action),
and hashes the engine with `nix hash file`. Supported systems are `x86_64-linux`,
`aarch64-linux`, and `aarch64-darwin`. Generation rejects known Intel macOS
grouped runner labels; custom runners must pass the system guard before
provisioning. Grouped configuration cannot override reserved `SIMIT_CI_*`,
`SIMIT_NIX_*`, or `INSTALLABLES` inputs.

The pinned engine closure is cached via GitHub Actions under
`simit-engine-v2-<revision>-<os>-<arch>` so group jobs evaluate the pin instead
of recompiling Simit each time. Provisioning, source-revision, and
executable-digest evidence stay unchanged, and misses or unreadable entries
build normally. Like `cache_installables`, entries carry the trust of the
repository's default-branch runs. Restore, import, and export run in every job
and branch inside their scripts; only cache save keeps a workflow condition,
because an action cannot be script-guarded.

`simit ci nix-group` reads generated environment lists or
`--spec <file> --results <directory>`; `simit::ci_runtime::group::execute` uses
the same typed contract. A JSON spec uses schema `simit.nix-group-spec.v1` with
`members`, `plan`, `check_systems`, `limits`, `post_build`, `post_build_always`,
and optional `fresh_installables`. Unknown fields, invalid membership, and
unsupported Nix flags fail before Nix runs. The results directory must already
exist and contain no prior group receipt or member evidence.

`simit.nix-group.v1` receipts preserve source/tree/run/attempt/event, ordered
results, hook statuses, and numbered member directories. `fresh_execution`
appears only for fresh members: each must materialize with valid output JSON,
then pass current-worker `--rebuild` with an empty `builders` override so remote
builders cannot replace local execution. Ordinary materialization never counts
as fresh acceptance. Fresh evidence keeps the transport filenames: `build.log`
(materialization), `materialization-result.json`, `fresh-build.log` (rebuild),
and `result.json` (final result). Malformed output and failed builds/hooks fail
the group while remaining members still run. Dispatch and process-limit failures
record status 125; Unix signals preserve negative v1 codes (for example `-9` for
SIGKILL). Member stdout/stderr and hook outputs are stored in separate files,
and failed admission observations surface actionable stderr in the CLI
diagnostic.

Before evidence writes, subprocess output caps at 16 MiB stdout and 64 MiB
stderr per command, with a six-hour maximum process lifetime (workflow timeouts
still apply). Unix cancellation halts execution and terminates the active
process group without starting later members. Accepted hooks up to 1 MiB run
from retained `.script` files to avoid per-argument limits. The workflow writes
a private JSON spec via a shell builtin rather than environment strings, and its
diagnostic fallback uses the same private-file transport. A small Bash wrapper
preserves `bash -c` argument identity, stdin, and trailing newlines. The compact
JSON spec (including escapes) must fit within 16 MiB; generation, library
admission, and the CLI reader enforce the same budget, rejecting oversized
combinations before writes or runtime effects even if each hook fits 1 MiB.
Generated grouped workflows must also stay within GitHub's 500,000-byte file
limit (counting embedded specs, repeated diagnostic fallbacks, YAML escaping,
and transport steps); overflow rejects before writing project files.

The CLI requires a nonempty `--results` or `SIMIT_NIX_BUILD_RESULTS` directory
and rejects missing or empty inputs before execution. Without `--spec`, it reads
fresh members from `SIMIT_NIX_FRESH` (JSON array) or
`SIMIT_NIX_FRESH_INSTALLABLES`; if both are set, their decoded lists must agree,
and invalid or conflicting values reject before dispatch or writes. The evidence
root cannot contain a prior receipt, inventory, coverage manifest, or numbered
member entries: the runtime rejects interrupted and fallback-only attempts
(including out-of-range member indices) before Git/Nix dispatch or evidence
writes; use a fresh evidence root rather than mixing attempts. Output-reader startup
failures use the same dispatch-failure path and clean up started readers and
child processes. Embedders call `execute_with` with a caller-owned
`Cancellation` token and `Runner`; the library installs no process-global signal
handlers. The CLI holds one cancellation flag across its lifetime (including
between subprocesses) and checks it before every dispatch.

The shell-only diagnostic fallback stays cancellation-aware, runs after setup,
provisioning, or admission failure, and uses completion markers to prevent
duplicate collection. The native integration suite exercises the generated
invocation and fallback against the packaged CLI at controlled Nix boundaries,
replacing the authored Python group harness while other Python fixtures keep
their packaging inputs until migrated.

Execution receipts are local evidence, not forge authority. Historical Python
v1 receipts remain readable, but new Rust source needs its own original-attempt
hosted qualification; offline integrity checks do not prove current provider
acceptance, merge readiness, or publication authorization.

### Native dependency stream admission

`simit::ci_runtime::dependencies` ports the reviewed export-stream admission
boundary from signed Simit source `a9874535107dd6cf335ab7c4bdfd9a9252c0c691`.
Its `ArchiveAdmission` inputs must come from separately validated source/run
provenance and fresh dependency/qualification evaluation; they express byte and
inventory expectations, not qualification authority. The transport workflow's
provenance/evaluation/export policy adapters remain a separate migration slice.

`admit_archive` verifies archive size and checksum while copying compressed
bytes into a private descriptor, decompresses only that checksum-bound snapshot
into a second anonymous descriptor, and parses the **entire** strict Nix writer
grammar before returning a one-use `VerifiedArchive`. Both descriptors are mode
`0600` and unlinked on Unix, so modifying or replacing the original archive
after admission cannot alter imported bytes.

The record set must exactly match the admitted closure, include every evaluated
dependency root, and exclude all qualification outputs. Paths and deriver
metadata must use canonical `/nix/store` syntax, with sorted, unique references
wholly inside the closure, zero legacy signature framing, and EOF immediately
after the terminal marker with no remaining bytes. Limits cover 100,000 paths,
1,000,000 nodes and references, bounded strings/byte budgets, and streamed
64 KiB reads.

Importer compatibility matches Nix **2.34.8** `src/libutil/archive.cc`: node
depth strictly below **64**, directory names at most **255 bytes**, and symlink
targets at most **4095 bytes**. Any invalid value rejects the entire stream
(even in a later record) before import. Directory names sort as raw bytes
(including non-UTF-8). ASCII case aliases within a directory are rejected on all
platforms before import so Darwin's case-hack rewrites cannot collide with real
entries.

`VerifiedArchive::restore` runs one `nix-store --import` from the rewound
validated descriptor, then verifies admitted paths and observes evaluated roots;
nonzero import/verification status emits no successful receipt. All restore
command batches are prepared before import against a 96 KiB combined
argv/environment budget (including terminators and pointer tables) with path
batches capped at 60 KiB. Commands inherit the same frozen, accounted
environment; oversized environments fail before store mutation. The envelope
leaves at least 32 KiB below supported Linux's 128 KiB exec floor and 160 KiB
below Darwin's 256 KiB limit for platform/interpreter overhead. The compressed
envelope uses checked arithmetic matching the producer's default zlib bound
(`maximum + (maximum >> 12) + (maximum >> 14) + (maximum >> 25) + 1 MiB`).
These library checks do not complete the transport or custody adapters'
source/provider admission or zero-Nix-before-byte-admission gates. `consume` accepts a caller-owned
importer with the same descriptor and one-use lifetime. Restoration receipts
always set `qualification_execution: false`; fresh checks still require
current-worker rebuilds.

Protocol sources:

- [Nix export/import framing](https://github.com/NixOS/nix/blob/adbf23e8184bbbe8d786aad1f362443b6542e0a4/src/libstore/export-import.cc)
- [Nix 2.34.8 importer grammar and limits](https://github.com/NixOS/nix/blob/2.34.8/src/libutil/archive.cc)

### Primary-only regeneration

Regenerate verification and native-build workflows from persisted policy during
a dependency migration:

```sh
simit init ci --primary-only --check --diff
simit init ci --primary-only
simit init ci --primary-only --check --diff
```

This scope covers member/aggregate CI (including independent lanes), native Nix
matrices, and prebuild workflows. Publisher, release, Pages, and review
workflows stay byte-for-byte unchanged along with `simit.toml`, release trust
roots, and README badges. `--check` reports drift only within this scope. Full
generation remains the default; run its separate drift gate when changing
publication config. `--primary-only` cannot be combined with other scope
selectors.

Project templates remain a separate owner regardless of basename
(`ci-release.yaml` and `build-release.yaml` do not become primary CI). Scoped
generation validates template paths and destination protections without loading
or rendering template, publisher, or review sources. After a mapping is removed,
its output files retain their markers until full generation retires them.
Primary cleanup still retires obsolete marked built-in CI workflows while
preserving hand-owned files. This scope does not create policy files like
`deny.toml`, and printed repair commands keep `--primary-only` plus the
effective platform/provider (including Crow format overrides).

### Project-owned workflow templates

Projects with specialized Actions jobs can render their own templates alongside
built-in Simit jobs:

```toml
[ci.workflow_templates]
".github/workflows/tests.yml" = ".simit/templates/tests.yml"

[ci.workflow_variables]
runner = "${{ github.event.repository.fork && 'ubuntu-24.04' || 'ubuntu-latest-32-core' }}"
```

Reference variables with `@simit(runner)@`. Simit performs single-pass literal
substitution, preserving GitHub `${{ ... }}` expressions and shell syntax with
no recursion or implicit env reads. Undefined variables and invalid rendered
YAML fail before writes. Keep credentials as runtime Actions secret references,
never literals in templates or config.

`simit init ci` renders declared templates, marks outputs as generated, and
persists mappings and variables; `--check --diff` and registry auditing share
this renderer so edits to outputs, templates, or variables surface as drift.
Removing a mapping retires files carrying both Simit generation and template
markers (even after leading project comments) while leaving unrelated workflows
project-owned. Collisions with built-in or release workflows, out-of-repo
paths, and mismatched Actions platforms fail validation. Template contents do
not feed into built-in check, package, or runner inference, and built-in
generated workflows cannot serve as template sources: templates must remain
project-owned inputs rather than snapshots of outputs from an earlier run.

Keep template sources outside Actions workflow directories or use a
non-workflow extension such as `.yaml.in` so they do not execute directly. File
identity checks cover both Actions workflow directories, blocking hard-linked
aliases. Every source and destination component must be portable (no Windows
device names, reserved characters, or trailing dots/spaces), validated before
filesystem resolution. Destinations must be files with directory parents;
before writing, Simit rejects directory or symlink destinations, hard-linked
aliases, and portable case/normalization collisions (Unicode canonical
normalization and full case folding across composed/decomposed spellings)
against template sources, planned outputs, or differently spelled active
project workflows (declaring the exact existing path keeps explicit adoption of
an existing project workflow). Filesystem case/normalization alias matching
excludes symlink endpoints. Outputs replace their directory entries
atomically—preserving existing permissions and leaving unrelated hard-linked
files untouched. Project-owned templates support GitHub and Forgejo Actions
(including exact-only Nix qualification) without replacing project test or
permission policies.

When importing upstream CI, keep presets in template sources and express
fork-specific policy via variables; apply upstream updates to sources and
regenerate instead of editing outputs.

### Provider-review merge gate

`canix-toolbelt` owns provider review, durable request accounting, and guarded
merging. When configured, Simit generates its trusted `review-policy`
coordinator separately from ordinary CI and the build-oriented `[review]`
controller:

```toml
[ci]
platform = "github"
provider = "actions"

[review_policy]
toolbelt_version = "0.2.0" # select a qualified, published stable release
app_id_secret = "REVIEW_POLICY_APP_ID"
app_private_key_secret = "REVIEW_POLICY_APP_PRIVATE_KEY"
credential_environment = "review-policy"
# Optional policy from the trusted default-branch checkout, JSON or Pkl:
# policy_path = "policy/review.json"
```

Generate and verify with `simit init ci --platform github` and
`simit init ci --platform github --check --diff`. Never enable a version before
independently verifying its crates.io publication.

Provision a **dedicated policy GitHub App**, install it on each enrolled
repository, store its ID/private key **only as secrets of the configured
credential environment**, and restrict that environment's deployment branch
policy to the exact default branch. Never create repository-level copies that
branch-controlled workflows could read outside the environment boundary; the
workflow's ref condition is an extra guard, while the platform-enforced
environment restriction protects the credential when a manual dispatch selects
an edited non-default-branch workflow. Verify that boundary before enabling the
coordinator. Unlike Greptile's installed App (which supplies review records),
the policy App authenticates the normalized check and needs only `Checks: write`,
`Contents: read`, `Pull requests: read`, `Issues: read`, and GitHub's mandatory
`Metadata: read`; do not grant contents write, administration write, or a merge
credential to the coordinator.

The workflow runs only on the default-branch ref, checks out its trusted event
SHA with credentials disabled, installs the locked registry engine, and never
executes PR source. PR/comment events reconcile single candidates (waiting up
to ten minutes without requesting another provider review); a ten-minute
scheduled sweep covers completed bot reviews, dismissals, and delayed feedback
across all open-PR pages (up to 5000 PRs, collected without waiting in batches
of twenty, allowing an active sweep to finish first; exceeding the bound fails
explicitly without claiming partial qualification). Findings block until source
fixes receive a fresh review or repository writers record exact-finding
evidence-backed dispositions.

Once the first check publishes, enable classic branch protection with strict
up-to-date checks and administrator enforcement, requiring `review-policy` bound
to its **dedicated App ID** plus the repository's actual required CI contexts
and human-approval policy. Do not bind the review context to the shared GitHub
Actions App: PR-controlled workflows can otherwise impersonate that context.
Missing protection, absent credentials, unsupported rulesets/merge queues, and
missing or failed CI all block merge.

Run `canix-toolbelt review ensure --pr URL`, investigate and fix confirmed
findings, re-run ensure after each head change, then run
`canix-toolbelt merge --pr URL --apply` for an authorized merge (or
`canix repo review` / `canix repo merge` once its qualified release is
installed). A `ready` receipt never replaces live merge revalidation.

### Rust feature coverage and MSRV environments

Rust Actions workflows honor `ci.all_features` for tests and Clippy in Cargo and
Nix runtimes, including split-runner jobs and crates.io publishers. Packages
with features also run `--no-default-features` (catching libraries whose
optional CLI is omitted by default).

With `ci.with_msrv = true`, Cargo jobs install and select the declared
`package.rust-version`; Nix jobs enter `devShells.<system>.msrv` and check
`rustc --version` matches before compiling all targets with the configured
feature policy. A default-shell alias to a newer compiler does not satisfy the
MSRV gate.

Nix format checks run `formatter.<system>` (from `meta.mainProgram`, `pname`,
or the derivation name). Treefmt runs with `--ci`; custom formatters run
without assumed arguments, preserve any nonzero exit status, and fail on any
tracked, index, or untracked changes. Missing executables fail the gate. Only
projects without a flake formatter fall back to shell treefmt, and then Cargo
formatting when treefmt is absent.

Rust flakes generated by `simit init flake` include `msrv` when Cargo declares
a minimum version. Full canonical generation also manages
`rust-toolchain-msrv.toml` (normalized version, minimal profile), read as a
source file rather than `builtins.toFile` (which does not materialize its
result during read-only no-build evaluation). Commit it with the flake; parity
checks reject missing or stale versions, while hooks-only and custom modes keep
project-owned manifests. Full canonical regeneration also migrates recognized
prior inline MSRV bindings before accepting hook wiring (reported as drift by
full checks), but leaves modified or dynamic inline manifests for manual
migration rather than dropping extra settings. Existing/custom flakes must
expose the same shell contract; hooks-only mode leaves their shells
project-owned. Commit `nix/rust-toolchain-msrv.toml` with the flake for
read-only evaluation. Use Harbor's `lib.rust.mkToolchain` with an exact-version
manifest and `mkCross`/`mkDevShells`, clear inherited nightly-only `RUSTFLAGS`
and `CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS` in stable/MSRV shells, and include native build
dependencies in the MSRV shell.

Generated native Rust, cross Rust, and Python flakes consume one exact-qualified
`github.com/caniko/harbor` input (`harbor.lib.rust`, `harbor.lib.python`, and
`harbor/<input>` follows). Project-owned flakes using standalone Harbor inputs
keep their wiring under hooks-only generation; migrate input, follows, and API
calls together before retiring a standalone source.

### Publishing mode

Rust CI and crates.io publishing are distinct modes. By default, `simit init ci`
emits ordinary CI only (even when a package has crates.io metadata: no
`publish-crate*.yaml` or `keys/maintainers.gpg`) unless release publishing is
explicitly enabled or inferred from existing generated release workflows.

Enable crates.io release workflows with:

```sh
simit init ci --platform forgejo --publish-crates
```

Persist the choice when a project owns release publishing:

```toml
[ci]
publish_crates = true
```

Use `--publish-crates=false` or `publish_crates = false` to stay CI-only even
with stale generated publish workflows. Release flags such as
`--with-artifacts`, `--with-homebrew`, `--with-chocolatey`, and `--with-scoop`
imply release mode.

Nix-only generation (including `[ci.nix_build].only = true`) rejects enabled
language/release options from CLI or `[ci]` (including `with_nextest`,
`with_msrv`, `with_audit`, `with_deny`, `with_docs`, `with_artifacts`, and
`with_pypi_publish`); move required checks into Nix installables or use
language CI. `publish_crates` is supported: a Nix-only Cargo workspace gets
per-member `publish-crate-*.yaml` and `trusted-publish-crate-*.yaml` without
language CI workflows; under `only = true`, the tag workflow omits
`nix flake check` to match primary CI. Members that depend on each other
require `publish_strategy = "coordinated"`, which emits the dependency-ordered
`publish-workspace.yaml` on GitHub instead. Explicit `--flag=false` disables
the matching option and persists that choice when generating; rejected requests
leave config and workflows untouched.

For a Forgejo Nix workspace with release artifacts and cargo-deny:

```sh
simit init ci --platform forgejo --runtime nix --runner atlas-nix-trusted \
  --workspace --with-artifacts --with-deny --check --diff
```

Per-member GitHub and Forgejo workflows use package-qualified job names (such as
`my-crate / test` and `my-crate / gate-integration`) so branch protection sees
distinct check names; regenerate and select the qualified names in branch
protection when adopting (single-package and aggregate names stay unchanged).
Homebrew CLI overrides work, but storing tap metadata in project config keeps
future checks shorter and reproducible.

## Flake-Integrated Rust Projects

`--runtime auto` picks Nix when `flake.nix` exposes meaningful project outputs
such as `packages`, `apps`, `checks`, `devShells`, NixOS/Home Manager modules,
or top-level `lib`; Cargo-only projects and placeholder flakes stay on Cargo CI.

For custom flakes, keep project-owned outputs intact and manage only hooks:

```sh
simit init flake --scope hooks-only
simit init ci --platform forgejo --runtime nix
```

## Focused Hosted Nix Builds

### Project-owned formatting

`simit init flake --scope full` wires the project treefmt policy into:

- `formatter.<system>` for `nix fmt`;
- `checks.<system>.formatting` for the uncached formatting gate;
- the development shell's packages for direct `treefmt` use;
- the pre-commit hook, using the same wrapper with `--ci`.

Rust and cross-platform shells use the pinned Rust formatter passed to
`nix/treefmt.nix`; Python shells use the same wrapper with their language
policy. Run `treefmt` inside `nix develop`, or run `nix fmt`.

Custom flakes own their shells and must include `treefmtEval.config.build.wrapper`
in `packages` (or Python `extraPackages`) beside
`pre-commit-check.enabledPackages`. `simit init flake --check --diff` flags
missing shell wiring; a comment or formatter output alone does not satisfy it.

Generated Nix CI runs the flake formatter with `--ci` and propagates evaluation,
build, and formatting failures. Projects with `nix/treefmt.nix`, `treefmt.toml`,
or `.treefmt.toml` must expose `formatter.<system>`; ambient treefmt or a
Rust-only check cannot substitute. Legacy Nix projects without treefmt policy
keep their Cargo fmt gate.

### Opt in to Simit's Nix setup action

Set `[ci].nix_setup_action_ref` to a 40-character lowercase `caniko/simit`
commit SHA containing `.github/actions/nix-setup/action.yml`. Generated GitHub
workflows then use that pinned action instead of calling the Cachix installer
directly. It takes no secret inputs; cache setup, Git transport, and publication
stay in the caller workflow. Omit it to keep existing output.

Declare the exact installables that qualify a feature in `[ci].nix_builds`;
GitHub Actions projects can configure this matrix independently of ordinary
checks and release jobs.

For native multi-architecture builds, set `[ci.nix_build.system_runners]`:

```toml
[ci.nix_build.system_runners]
"x86_64-linux" = "ubuntu-24.04"
"aarch64-linux" = "ubuntu-24.04-arm"
```

Every installable must name its system explicitly (e.g.
`.#checks.aarch64-linux.cargo-test`, `.#packages.x86_64-linux.server`,
`.#formatter.aarch64-linux`) and match a runner entry. Generation emits one job
per installable; on the runner, each job verifies OS/CPU identity independently
of Nix config, then checks the configured Nix system before project setup or
realization. Linux, Darwin, and FreeBSD kernels are recognized; unsupported
kernels fail closed. With `kvm = true`, KVM setup runs only on `x86_64-linux`
rows; ARM rows do not need `/dev/kvm`. `[ci].runner` still controls ordinary
language CI, and omitting the map keeps single-runner matrix behavior. Standard
`formatter.<system>`, `defaultPackage.<system>`, and `devShell.<system>` select
their system without a trailing name; output selectors (`^out`, `^out,dev`,
`^*`) stay intact because routing reads only the attribute path. If any mapped
worker needs the compatible Node 20 baseline, all rows use it regardless of
`[ci].runner`. PowerPC uname spellings (`ppc`, `ppcle`, `ppc64`, `ppc64le`)
normalize to Nix `powerpc` names.

`[ci.nix_build.groups]` also works with the map: each group must contain
installables for one system and runs on that system's runner (mixed-system
groups reject before writes), with the same hardware/Nix guard, x86 Linux-only
KVM condition, and per-member evidence/hooks. Native mappings currently cannot
combine with `dependency_installables` because the single dependency producer
does not support native per-system routing; that combination rejects before
writes rather than realizing foreign dependencies on one worker.

```toml
[ci]
platform = "github"
provider = "actions"
runtime = "nix"
runner = "ubuntu-24.04"
nix_builds = [
  ".#checks.x86_64-linux.client-runtime",
  ".#checks.x86_64-linux.managed-postgres-recovery",
]

[ci.nix_build]
only = true
timeout_minutes = 90
max_parallel = 1
max_jobs = 1
cores = 2
kvm = true
capture_results = true
artifact_retention_days = 14
extra_setup = ["python3 ci/prepare-input-access.py"]
post_build = ["python3 ci/retain-receipts.py"]
post_build_always = ["python3 ci/retain-diagnostics.py"]
artifact_paths = ["${{ runner.temp }}/receipts/**"]
required_secrets = ["FLAKE_SSH_KEY"]

[ci.nix_build.extra_env]
FLAKE_SSH_KEY = "${{ secrets.FLAKE_SSH_KEY }}"
```

Generate and check with `simit init ci --platform github --runtime nix` and
`simit init ci --check --diff`. `only = true` supports flake-only, Rust, and
Python flake projects: it emits `nix-builds.yaml` without a broad flake-check
workflow, retiring obsolete Simit-managed primary CI while keeping project-owned
workflows. It cannot combine with `components`, `nix_system_runners`, or
language release flags other than `publish_crates`. It coexists with
`[prebuild]` (which publishes its own `[prebuild].nix_builds` subset). Without
`only`, coexistence is supported only on a GitHub Actions primary, and only when
`[prebuild].nix_builds` selects a subset or `[ci.nix_build]` sets an option;
otherwise prebuild realizes every `[ci].nix_builds` entry itself. Rust
workspaces resolve this from the workspace root (even when invoked from member
directories). Select all required Rust checks explicitly as Nix installables in
this mode; Rust and Python projects can also use the other matrix options
alongside ordinary CI.

The matrix runs on branch pushes, pull requests, and dispatches. Its push
trigger sets only `branches`, excluding tag pushes; channel release workflows
keep their own triggers and policy.

Nested environment and setup apply only to the build matrix. Bind each required
secret to the same-named variable via `${{ secrets.NAME }}` in `extra_env`;
preflight fails on missing secrets without printing values (fork PRs receive no
repository secrets, so credential-dependent jobs fail preflight rather than
claiming qualification). `required_env` runs after setup so setup can create
credential files. Keep private-input credentials out of global `[ci].extra_env`
and release jobs.

KVM setup requires a GitHub-hosted Linux runner with `/dev/kvm`. Matrix builds
pass `--no-update-lock-file`; `max_jobs` and `cores` bound realization, and
`max_parallel` bounds matrix concurrency. Validated bounds: timeout 1–360
minutes, parallelism 1–256, jobs 1–1024, cores 0–1024 (0 = all cores), and
artifact retention 1–90 days.

With `capture_results = true`, `$SIMIT_NIX_BUILD_RESULTS` points to a
job-specific runner temp directory containing `revision`, `installable`,
`build.log`, and Nix's `result.json` (derivation and output paths). Nix's
failure status is preserved while streaming and retaining its diagnostics.
`post_build` commands run after successful realization; they can read
`result.json` and copy receipts/VM reports into the evidence directory, and
must fail if an expected receipt is missing. The pinned upload action runs even
on failure and includes `artifact_paths`. Artifacts hold evidence, not Nix
store closures; empty or partial results after failure are not passing receipts.

Use `post_build_always` (`if: ${{ !cancelled() }}`, before upload) for
diagnostics that must run after failed setup or builds; commands must tolerate
missing or partial logs/results. Collector failures fail the job, and passing
collectors never mask build failures. Both post-build lists require
`capture_results = true`; keep receipt validation in `post_build`. Omitting
`[ci.nix_build]` preserves default matrix behavior.

### Shared-store Nix groups

Rust projects on GitHub Actions can enable `[ci].independent_lanes = true`. The
`rust` lane keeps format, test, quality, docs, generator, and package steps
using the project's runtime; required-gate jobs qualify the same immutable PR
head. Lanes start independently on the same push/PR triggers. Step-runner
overrides and `om_ci` are unsupported with independent lanes.

With `runtime = "nix"`, `evaluation` evaluates the flake on all systems without
building and `realization` builds all flake checks; `nix_flake_check = false`
omits only `realization` (establish replacement check and production-output
coverage first). With `runtime = "cargo"`, `rust` runs native Cargo without
Nix; set `nix_flake_check = true` with a root `flake.nix` to add the flake
lanes (independent of explicit Nix gates, `nix-builds.yaml`, and `[prebuild]`,
and also qualifying release-plz revisions before publish). Required contexts
change from `test` to `rust`, `evaluation`, and (when enabled) `realization`
(with member prefixes if applicable); enroll every applicable lane and group
context before retiring `test`.

`[ci.nix_build.groups]` partitions every `ci.nix_builds` entry into named jobs
so related packages and checks share a fresh hosted runner's Nix store and
build common dependencies once within that job. Membership must be complete,
nonempty, and disjoint, with `capture_results = true`. Grouped jobs provision
an independently pinned native Rust engine; the separate dependency-transport
adapter provisions Python 3.12 via a pinned setup action for its producer and
consumer steps (including on custom runners). Omitting `timeout_minutes` keeps
the runner default timeout.

```toml
[ci.nix_build]
capture_results = true
max_parallel = 4
max_jobs = 1
cores = 2
check_systems = ["x86_64-linux"]

[ci.nix_build.groups]
pinentry = [".#pinentry", ".#checks.x86_64-linux.pinentry"]
network = [".#checks.x86_64-linux.network"]
```

The example assumes those are all declared installables and all checks on the
selected system. `check_systems` discovers all check derivations (including
checks supplied by imported flake modules) before realization and rejects
unassigned checks. Each group retains a source-bound coverage manifest plus
per-installable results, exit statuses, and logs; a failed member fails the job
while remaining members still collect diagnostics. Post-build hooks run per
successful member with `INSTALLABLE` and `SIMIT_NIX_BUILD_RESULTS` set to that
member's numbered evidence directory. Grouped hook bodies cannot contain
`${{ ... }}`, because GitHub would expand them into retained spec and script
files (bind via `extra_env` and read shell variables instead), and `extra_env`
cannot override `SIMIT_DEPENDENCY_*`. Diagnostic hooks run for every member,
including after setup/admission failure, with a shell fallback for skipped
members and completion markers preventing duplicate collection; hook failures
fail the group while later members still run. Transport admission checks stay
enforced under Python optimization. Grouped jobs report `build (<group>)`
contexts; qualify the new evidence and migrate required contexts together
before retiring a monolithic flake-check gate.

Simit's `Qualify native grouped execution` workflow exercises the production
engine on fresh `aarch64-linux` and `aarch64-darwin` hosted workers: each job
verifies actual hardware before provisioning, builds the event-head engine, and
runs its generated native guard, immutable bootstrap, group invocation, and
diagnostic fallback across cold materialization and warm-store rebuilds
(requiring current-worker builder markers, ordered v1 receipts, passing hooks,
and no duplicate fallback). Artifacts retain source hashes, derivation, engine
digest, generated workflow, and per-state evidence. Only passing
original-attempt jobs and independently verified artifacts establish platform
acceptance for that exact source; this workflow does not enroll consumer
variables or required contexts.

### Completion-driven producer custody

`[ci.custody]` generates a trusted default-branch `workflow_run` observer.
Enroll workflow names, source paths, required job names, and required artifact
names. Branch/PR producers must use original attempt 1; the observer never
reruns producers or checks out/executes their source or artifacts.

```toml
[ci.custody]
repository = "owner/repository"
producer_attempt = 1
status_context = "simit/producer-custody"

[ci.custody.producers.CI]
workflow = ".github/workflows/ci.yaml"
jobs = ["rust", "evaluation"]

[ci.custody.producers."Nix installable builds"]
workflow = ".github/workflows/nix-builds.yaml"
jobs = ["build (network)", "build (pinentry)"]
artifacts = ["nix-build-0", "nix-build-1"]
```

Policies default to `strict-v1`. Set `protocol = "sealed-v2"` in `[ci.custody]`
to opt into [sealed-original custody](../ci-sealed-custody.md) (immediate
capture, complete evidence sealed as immutable artifacts, and independent
verification of exact capsules before aggregation and source-head reporting);
see that page for v2 details. The following describes the default `strict-v1`
observer.

GitHub runs `workflow_run` from the default branch whenever **any** listed
workflow completes, so install the observer on the default branch before testing
candidates. Earlier completions may record pending observations; the last
aggregates all enrolled producers for the same source head, branch, and event.
Duplicate identities, nonoriginal attempts, missing jobs/artifacts,
failed/skipped required jobs, and incomplete custody cannot succeed. Because
display names are not unique, positively identified workflow files outside
enrolled paths are ignored before creating a target or queue (repeated in
capture and report without reading stale receipts), whereas an enrolled path
with a wrong name or ref still fails admission and revokes its target.
Admission and bounded-capture checks raise explicit errors and stay active
under Python optimization, and failed revalidation revokes prior success in
both ordinary and optimized modes.

The observer binds each workflow definition via GitHub's native
[`WorkflowRun.file` / `WorkflowRunFile`](https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/reference/actions#workflowrunfile)
record. Its repository, path, parent run, attempt, event, and check-suite
repository must match the original, and `repositoryFileUrl` must name an
immutable 40-hex commit. Custody fetches and hashes the enrolled file at that
revision, retaining the native response, commit, Git blob metadata, and bytes;
each producer row records `workflow_revision`, `workflow_tree`, and
`source_workflow_sha256` (while receipt `head` / `tree` keep the source-head
identity). Raw REST `head_sha`, checkout logs, reusable workflows, and PR merge
refs do not substitute for executed-file proof (critical when the base
introduced or changed a workflow absent or different at the PR head).
Unavailable records or mutable URLs fail closed at the established target;
capture-final and post-upload report requery the record and revoke success in
the same stable context on revision drift. Native file records at raw head
count as explicit provider proof, not source-head inference. Installed-token
GraphQL access remains a live acceptance gate.

The observer retains original jobs, log archives, and required artifact bytes,
hashing archives without extraction. Limits: 512 MiB shared wire budget for
capture/API downloads, 512 MiB retained files, 512 MiB total archive expansion,
256 requests, 256 retained files, 10,000 archive members, and a six-minute
capture deadline. Downloads and hashes stream in 64 KiB chunks; oversized or
stalled downloads terminate and reap child processes. Before creating a ZIP
reader, custody scans central-directory records under a 16 MiB directory bound,
remaining member/expansion budgets, and the deadline so forged footer counts
cannot bypass limits. Stored and deflated archives (including ZIP64) are
supported; other compression methods fail admission before any member
decompression. Enrollment allows at most 100 jobs/artifacts total, and rendered
workflows must fit within GitHub's
[500 KB workflow-file limit](https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud@latest/actions/reference/limits#workflow-file-size)
(500,000 UTF-8 bytes including repeated policy/program text and YAML/JSON
escaping); oversized policies reject before reconciliation or persistence
(shorten enrolled names/inventories to fit). Capture budget failures preserve
the established failure-reporting target.

Both capture and upload must finish before posting success. Reporting is
idempotent and targets the producer commit (not the observer's default-branch
SHA) under `<status_context>/<event>/<target-sha256>`, using the full SHA-256
of the canonical target identity (repository IDs/normalized names, event, exact
case-sensitive head branch, and for PRs: PR ID, number, base repository ID, and
exact base ref). Prefix max is 22 UTF-8 bytes (100-byte composed-context
contract). Different PRs or bases at the same commit get distinct contexts;
enroll them before replacing protection. Repository names compare
case-insensitively per GitHub's owner/repository naming rules.

PR custody requires exactly one valid provider PR association matching head
SHA/ref and repository IDs; missing, ambiguous, or malformed associations fail
without falling back to a branch target. Discovery, selected details,
capture-final, and report-time revalidation bind the stable identity and
head/base SHA snapshots (snapshot equality is conservative admission of
observed API data, not authenticated historical base provenance); excluding
base SHA from the status key lets later changes revoke the same target.

A token-free, contents-read identity job derives the full target digest before
collection. Collection keys job-level concurrency on that digest plus head SHA
(isolating branches, PRs, base refs, and case-distinct refs); pending
replacement within one target observes the same enrolled producer set. The
strict protocol also groups workflow runs by producer workflow id, source
repository, head SHA, event, branch, and first associated PR so only the newest
pending completion queues a runner (workflow id prevents unenrolled same-named
workflows from replacing pending enrolled ones). Because Actions groups ignore
case and see only the first PR, rare colliding targets lose a pending run and
that target's status stays missing until its next completion (failing closed);
sealed custody keeps one run per completion. Collect reserves 25 minutes:
six-minute capture, five-minute upload, six-minute report lookups, and a
90-second status POST; reporting runs after failed upload or lookup exhaustion
to publish failure when the completion target was safely established.

Same-repository branch/PR custody is supported; signed-tag release attempt
policy and fork custody require separately qualified enrollment. Collect holds
only contents/actions/checks read (`checks: read` covers private-repo
check-suite proofs) and statuses write; identity holds only contents read with
no token env. This establishes observation custody, not execution acceptance—keep
native test/build contexts and consumer validation authoritative, and qualify
default-branch installation, completion ordering, source-head reporting, and
all-producer aggregation using the
[installed-observer acceptance procedure](../ci-custody-acceptance.md) (both
completion orders, isolation, and live failure/revocation) before replacing a
waiting collector.

Simit's own enrollment observes `CI/test` and a short source-bound
`Custody qualification fixture` that uploads inert Python text (hashed without
execution) to exercise pending-to-complete aggregation. Candidate runs before
default-branch merge qualify only the generator and fixture; retain merged
observer and subsequent branch/PR events to qualify installation, reporting, and
ordering.

### CI dependency reuse

`[ci.cache]` declares public, credential-free HTTPS substituters and signing
keys for CI separately from release publication. An explicit empty table
disables inherited release-cache settings; omitting it preserves inheritance.
Forgejo Actions applies these settings to preinstalled Nix while keeping
existing `NIX_CONFIG`. Release publication keeps its own cache policy, and
`with_nix_cargo_cache = true` continues to control the native Cargo cache.

```toml
[ci.cache]
substituters = ["https://cache.example.org"]
trusted_public_keys = ["cache.example.org:PUBLIC_KEY_BASE64"]

[ci.nix_build]
dependency_installables = [".#ci-patched-zellij"]
dependency_max_mib = 2048
fresh_installables = [".#checks.x86_64-linux.pinentry-runtime"]
```

Dependency transport requires groups and discovered `check_systems`. It builds
only selected build inputs in a separate fresh worker and exports their complete
closure to a same-run artifact. Enroll bare local attributes (e.g.
`.#ci-patched-zellij`) so transport builds all outputs; explicit `^out`, `^dev`,
and `^*` selectors reject before generation in both dependency enrollment and
transport-enabled qualification plans (non-transport workflows keep existing
selector behavior). Transport-enabled plans also require bare `.#attribute`
local derivations so remote/path references cannot drift between producer,
import, and group build. Both producer and consumers inherit the runner's
default timeout when `timeout_minutes` is omitted.

Compressed-size budgets include zlib's worst-case DEFLATE expansion plus gzip
framing; export checks the bound before marking an archive complete, import
checks it before store effects, and both streams enforce separate uncompressed
limits throughout. Import checks compressed size, checksum, and decompressed
budget before derivation evaluation (which can instantiate store objects or
trigger IFD). Compressed bytes are privately snapshotted so checksum and
decompression read the same snapshot even if the downloaded inode changes;
admitted decompressed bytes stay in one unlinked mode-0600 spool descriptor
through source/graph checks and import.

Consumers verify commit/tree, lock bytes, repository, run, attempt, expected
derivations/output paths, checksum, and budget, then parse the full Nix
export/NAR stream without extraction. Actual records must match the admitted
closure with all references inside it; duplicate, missing, extra, malformed,
truncated, or trailing records reject before import. Limits cap paths,
references, tree depth/nodes, and control fields, streaming payloads in 64 KiB
chunks: NAR depth < 64, entry names <= 255 bytes, symlink targets <= 4095 bytes
per [Nix 2.34.8 importer limits](https://github.com/NixOS/nix/blob/2.34.8/src/libutil/archive.cc),
checked across the entire stream before import. ASCII case aliases within a
directory reject on all platforms to prevent Darwin's `~nix~case~hack~`
collisions (unrelated suffix names and separate directories still work). Parsing
follows [Nix's export framing](https://github.com/NixOS/nix/blob/adbf23e8184bbbe8d786aad1f362443b6542e0a4/src/libstore/export-import.cc)
and [NAR writer grammar](https://github.com/NixOS/nix/blob/adbf23e8184bbbe8d786aad1f362443b6542e0a4/doc/manual/src/protocols/nix-archive.md).
Legacy export signatures are rejected (archive integrity is not producer
authority). Aliases of discovered checks or qualification outputs are refused,
and a failed producer blocks consumers while keeping its diagnostics.

Artifacts bind to the exact run **and attempt**. After a consumer failure, use
**Re-run all jobs** so the producer runs in the new attempt; **Re-run failed
jobs** can retain a prior-attempt producer whose artifact consumers reject, with
no cross-attempt or cross-run fallback.

`kvm = true` enables hosted KVM on both producer and consumers before setup or
builds. Export and post-import verification check complete argument vectors
against the current worker's `ARG_MAX` (charging inherited env and pointer
arrays with platform headroom), rejecting closures before export, or before any
import when verification would exceed the consumer's limit. Independently
terminated export streams are never concatenated.

`fresh_installables` first materialize cold outputs and dependencies normally,
then require `--rebuild` on the current worker (so uncached checks can run
twice; materialization alone is never acceptance). Direct aliases and transitive
qualification outputs are rejected from dependency transport before
export/import. Keep VMs and runtime checks in `fresh_installables`, measuring
export, download/import, and cache-hit costs against end-to-end latency.

`cache_installables` reuses heavy local build inputs across runs (such as a
patched VM kernel). It requires groups and bare `.#attribute` derivations that
are not qualification outputs, `checks`, or transported dependencies:

```toml
[ci.nix_build]
cache_installables = [".#nixosTests.x86_64-linux.vm.nodes.machine.boot.kernelPackages.kernel"]
```

Each group resolves entries to exact derivations and restores GitHub Actions
cache key `simit-nix-input-v1-<derivation hash>` with no restore keys (changed
inputs miss and rebuild). Hits import all outputs and their closure before the
group runs, failing the job if that closure contains an output of one of that
group's qualification members; unreadable entries are ignored. Afterward (even
on member failure), newly realized entries not restored are exported and saved
up to 4 GiB each. GitHub cache scoping applies (PRs read default-branch entries
and write only their own scope). Because imports skip signature checks, declare
only inputs whose producers you trust as much as the default branch.

Generated GitHub Nix matrices and aggregate Rust CI isolate push and PR runs so
opening a PR does not cancel its exact-head push run; newer revisions supersede
older runs within each stream and forks stay isolated. Cancelled predecessors
remain failures and cannot substitute for required producers. Existing
`separate_events` settings remain accepted, including under custody.

Nix matrices qualify branch pushes by default. Set
`[ci.nix_build].push_tags = ["**"]` to qualify every tag push (including when
adopting a workflow with an unfiltered `push:` trigger), or use selective
patterns and ordered exclusions such as `push_tags = ["v*", "!v*-preview"]`
(nonempty lists need at least one positive pattern). Tag patterns survive
regeneration and drift checks, and omitting them keeps the branch-only default.
Tag pushes remain separate from same-named branches and pull requests.

## Required Integration Gates

Custom flakes declare required gates without hand-editing generated YAML:

```toml
[[ci.required_gates]]
id = "gel-integration"
run = "nix run .#test-gel"
timeout_minutes = 30

[[ci.required_gates]]
id = "gel-check"
run = "nix flake check --no-write-lock-file"
timeout_minutes = 30
env = { GEL_FIXTURE = "local" }
```

Each gate has a stable `id`, a single-line `run` (`nix run`, `nix build`, or
`nix flake check` for flake targets), a bounded `timeout_minutes` (1–360,
default 30), and scoped `env`. Gates render as `gate-<id>` CI jobs (push/PR
triggers, once per run) and as credential-free prerequisites in the coordinated
publisher at the exact signed revision; any failure blocks publication. Keep
