gate setup in `run`/`env` (never global `[ci].extra_setup`) so publish/artifact
jobs do not inherit test-only services or credentials, and keep release secrets
(`CRATES_IO_API_TOKEN`, minisign, etc.) out of gate `env`—they belong only in
independent default-branch upload jobs in the protected `simit-crates-io`
environment.

Omit `runtime` to keep the existing CI and publication setup, or set `cargo`
(native Rust), `nix` (Nix setup), or `shell` (neither). Simit runs `run` verbatim without wrapping
Nix gates in `nix develop`, so remote installables need no local flake.
Explicit-runtime gates get separate jobs in GitHub hosted releases and the
trusted crate publisher; release-plz runs gates in its shared job, so overrides
must match the project runtime. Crow CI rejects `[[ci.required_gates]]` and
allows `[[ci.manual_gates]]` only. Non-GitHub hosted releases disallow runtime
overrides for required gates. Forgejo Actions uses preinstalled Nix (requiring
Nix CI on a Nix runner for Nix gates) and does not run required gates during
crate publication, so combining them with `publish_crates = true` is rejected.

GitHub Actions renders `[[ci.manual_gates]]` into `manual-gates.yaml`
(`workflow_dispatch`); Crow renders one `.crow/manual-<id>.yaml` per gate
(`manual` trigger, allowing `runtime = "cargo"` or `"nix"`). Both enforce
`timeout_minutes`. Manual gates are drift-checked but never run on push/PR or
block publication. IDs must be unique across both lists.

On GitHub Actions, gates can retain diagnostic files after success or failure:

```toml
[ci.required_gates.artifacts]
name = "gel-evidence"
paths = ["target/evidence/", "e2e/test-results/"]
retention_days = 14
```

Place this table immediately after its gate. Names must be valid and unique
across gates, with no surrounding whitespace in names or paths (the upload
action trims inputs). Retention defaults to seven days (1–90). Uploads use
`always()` gated on the step's outcome so failed gates upload evidence while
skipped or not-started gates cannot publish stale files; missing files warn, and
gate failure still blocks publication. Uploads time out at five minutes using
the runner-compatible action version. Hidden files under selected paths are
included—exclude sensitive files explicitly even if dot-prefixed.

Artifact-bearing CI gates apply `timeout_minutes` to the command step and add
fifteen minutes for setup/upload, capping `timeout_minutes` at 345 minutes
(other gates keep 360). GitHub crates.io publication runs all gates once,
serially, in its first trusted verification job (source build and dependent
verification jobs do not repeat them), adding gate deadlines plus five minutes
per upload to its sixty-minute base budget reserved for setup, the workspace
lane, and packaging; hosted-release validation adds the same gate budget to ten
setup minutes. Configurations exceeding the shared publishing job limit of 360 minutes
are rejected (independent CI gates do not share this cap). Workflow/job
cancellation can still prevent uploads; this is diagnostic retention, not
external custody.

Relative paths resolve from the gate's source checkout (including isolated
signed-source verification). Absolute, tilde, and leading-expression paths
(`${{ runner.temp }}/evidence`) stay unchanged; isolated trusted verification
requires leading expressions to directly reference `runner.temp` or
`github.workspace`, whose values are absolute (put variable subdirectories after
a literal relative prefix like
`target/${{ vars.EVIDENCE_SUBDIR }}/report.xml`). Artifact expressions cannot
reference `env` because upload actions do not inherit candidate gate
environments (use literals or `runner`, `github`, or `vars`), and artifact
names and paths in credential-free publishing cannot reference GitHub secrets
or authentication contexts. Trusted crate publishers name gate artifacts
`<artifact-name>.<package-name>` (distinct from hyphenated crate archives),
hosted-release validation uses `gate.<artifact-name>` (avoiding
`release-<system>` and `flake-inputs-<system>`), and ordinary CI keeps the
declared name. Forgejo and Crow reject this GitHub-only option after CLI
overrides resolve; hosted release checks its effective release backend
independently of the CI default.

## Target-OS Smoke Tests

A Nix cross-build (such as a Windows `.exe` built on Linux) needs a real target
runner to prove it runs. `[[ci.target_smokes]]` builds an installable on the
Linux CI runner and runs a command against the output on a target-OS runner:

```toml
[[ci.target_smokes]]
id = "windows"
nix_build = ".#packages.x86_64-linux.sorrel-windows-smoke"
runner = "windows-2025"
shell = "pwsh"
run = "./smoke/windows.ps1"
timeout_minutes = 30
env = { SORREL_LOG = "info" }
artifacts = { name = "windows-smoke", paths = ["smoke-out/**"], retention_days = 7 }
```

| Field             | Default  | Meaning                                                         |
| ----------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`              | required | Unique, `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+`; names the jobs and the build artifact |
| `nix_build`       | required | Installable for `nix build` on the Linux CI runner              |
| `runner`          | required | Target runner label (same rules as `[ci].runner`)               |
| `shell`           | `bash`   | `bash` or `pwsh`                                                |
| `run`             | required | Single-line command run from the checked-out repository         |
| `timeout_minutes` | `30`     | Limit for `run`, 1-345; the job adds 15 minutes of overhead     |
| `env`             | `{}`     | Environment for `run` only                                      |
| `artifacts`       | none     | Same fields as gate artifacts; uploaded even when `run` fails   |

Each entry emits two jobs in `target-smokes.yaml` (same push/PR triggers,
concurrency, and read-only `contents` permission as ordinary CI):

1. `build-target-smoke-<id>` runs `nix build <nix_build> --out-link result` with
   shared Nix setup/substituters, copies the dereferenced output into
   `target-smoke-<id>/`, and uploads it via `actions/upload-artifact`.
2. `target-smoke-<id>` depends on the build job, checks out the repo on
   `runner`, downloads the output into `target-smoke-<id>/`, exports
   `SIMIT_TARGET_SMOKE_DIR` pointing at it, and runs `run` in `shell` against
   that output.

Require `target-smoke-<id>` as a status check. Because artifact upload drops
executable bits, smoke scripts should `chmod +x` binaries on macOS. Both Nix
and Rust GitHub CI emit the workflow; Python uv CI, Forgejo, GitLab, and Crow
reject the option with an error. The table persists in `simit.toml` and is
drift-checked by `simit init ci --check`; removing it deletes the workflow.

## Native Tests on Hosted Runners

Linux Nix CI runs `cargo test` on Linux; code with OS-specific behaviour (file
locking, paths, memory-mapped files) needs a real run on its target OS.
`[[ci.native_tests]]` runs `cargo test` natively without Nix on a hosted runner:

```toml
[[ci.native_tests]]
id = "windows"
runner = "windows-2025"
args = "--workspace --locked"
timeout_minutes = 60
toolchain = "stable"
env = { RUST_BACKTRACE = "1" }
setup = """
curl -fsSL -o driver.zip https://example.com/driver.zip
echo "DRIVER_DIR=$PWD/driver" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
"""
```

| Field             | Default                                                      | Meaning                                        |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `id`              | required                                                     | Unique, `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+`; names the job        |
| `runner`          | required                                                     | Runner label (same rules as `[ci].runner`)     |
| `args`            | `--workspace --locked`                                       | Single-line arguments after `cargo test`       |
| `timeout_minutes` | `60`                                                         | Limit for `cargo test`, 1-345; the job adds 15 |
| `toolchain`       | `channel` of `rust-toolchain.toml` if present, else `stable` | rustup toolchain name, e.g. `1.85.0`           |
| `env`             | `{}`                                                         | Environment for `cargo test` only              |
| `setup`           | none                                                         | Bash commands run once before `cargo test`     |

Each entry emits `native-test-<id>` in `native-tests.yaml` (same push triggers
honouring `push_branches`, pull-request triggers, concurrency, and read-only
`contents` permission as ordinary CI). It checks out the repo, installs the
toolchain via pinned `dtolnay/rust-toolchain`, runs any optional `setup` step
(`Setup <id>`, under `bash` with a 15 minute limit added to the job limit,
capping `timeout_minutes` at 330; export variables by appending `NAME=value`
lines to `$GITHUB_ENV` and pin/checksum downloads under read-only `contents`
with no secrets), and then runs `cargo test <args>` under `bash` (Git Bash on
Windows) with the step timeout. Require `native-test-<id>` as a status check.
No dependency cache is configured, so expect a cold Windows build and raise
`timeout_minutes` for large workspaces. Native tests are GitHub Actions only:
Python uv CI, Forgejo, GitLab, and Crow reject the option with an error. The
table persists in `simit.toml` and is drift-checked by `simit init ci --check`;
removing it deletes the workflow.

## Coordinated Workspace Publication

Member-scoped `publish-crate-<crate>.yaml` has no cross-crate ordering. For
lockstep workspaces that need prerequisites published before dependents, opt in
(GitHub Actions only in v1):

```toml
[ci]
workspace = true
workspace_strategy = "aggregate"
publish_crates = true
publish_strategy = "coordinated"
```

```sh
simit init ci --platform github --runtime nix --workspace --workspace-strategy aggregate --publish-crates --coordinated-publish
simit init ci --platform github --check --diff
```

Switching strategies removes only obsolete simit-owned outputs
(`publish-crate-*.yaml` / `trusted-publish-crate-*.yaml` vs
`publish-workspace.yaml` / `trusted-publish-workspace.yaml`), never handwritten
workflows. Forgejo, Crow, and GitLab fail explicitly.

Coordinated publication does not require aggregate CI: keep
`workspace_strategy = "members"` for per-member CI policies and set
`publish_strategy = "coordinated"` (`simit init ci --coordinated-publish` keeps
an existing workspace CI strategy).

GitHub tag workflows retain credential-free archives while independently trusted
`workflow_run` companions upload to crates.io. Enrollment requires a qualified
`vars.SIMIT_PUBLISHER_REVISION`, a default-branch-restricted `simit-crates-io`
environment, and removing tag-accessible publish secrets; see
[Release Integrity](release-integrity.md) before enabling this route.

Single-crate and coordinated publishers compare verified local archives against
the registry response before resuming an existing version (exact crate/version,
unyanked, matching SHA-256; missing, malformed, or conflicting records fail).
Both publication and checksum-matched recovery require bounded independent Cargo
fetches of the exact version, source, and checksum before succeeding.

Generated GitHub Pages deploys share the repository-wide `github-pages`
concurrency group across manual/push events and refs without canceling active
deploys; ordinary CI keeps event/ref-scoped concurrency.

## Non-Publishable Crates

Cargo exposes `publish = false` as an empty `publish` list, which Simit treats
as a hard crates.io opt-out:

- CI still runs tests, optional policy gates, and clippy for that package.
- CI skips `cargo package` for that package.
- Simit omits `publish-crate-<package>.yaml` for that package.

This lets workspace utilities like `xtask` depend on unpublished git-only
helpers, since `cargo package -p xtask` fails even though the crate is
intentionally not publishable. Delete stale generated `publish-crate-*.yaml`
files for `publish = false` members after regenerating CI (`--check` reports
them as `extra`).

## Cargo-Deny Policy

`--with-deny` causes generated workflows to install and run:

```sh
cargo deny check bans licenses sources
```

`deny.toml` is project-owned: Simit creates a conservative default if missing,
leaves existing files alone, and does not flag local license or source
allow-list edits as CI drift. Validate policy edits with the CI-pinned
`cargo-deny` version (a newer local `cargo-deny` may differ:
`cargo-deny 0.18.3` expects `GPL-3.0` rather than `GPL-3.0-only`):

```sh
CARGO_HOME=/tmp/simit-cargo-deny-0183
cargo install cargo-deny --locked --version 0.18.3
"$CARGO_HOME/bin/cargo-deny" check bans licenses sources
```

## Forgejo Nix Runtime Details

Forgejo Nix-runtime workflows set:

```yaml
env:
  NIX_CONFIG: "experimental-features = nix-command flakes"
  XDG_CACHE_HOME: "/tmp/.cache"
  CARGO_HOME: "/tmp/.cargo"
```

`CARGO_HOME` must be absolute because relative paths can panic `cargo install`
or misplace files in Forgejo/act containers. Workflows add `$CARGO_HOME/bin` to
`PATH` before installing optional Cargo tools there rather than assuming them on
the runner image. MSRV checks run via the dev shell rather than `cargo +<msrv>`
(Nix dev shells do not imply rustup):

```sh
nix develop -c cargo check --all-targets
```

### Nix-runtime Cargo cache

Projects with a substantial host-side Cargo gate can supply a project-owned
command while keeping `nix flake check`:

```toml
[ci]
check_command = "cargo xtask ci"
```

`check_command` replaces only the generic Cargo lane; Nix-runtime workflows
still run `nix flake check` by default. Projects with a focused Nix validation
workflow may opt out explicitly:

```toml
[ci]
check_command = "cargo run --locked -p syndb-ci -- ci"
nix_flake_check = false
```

Opt into registry and target caching for host-side Cargo gates:

```toml
[ci]
runtime = "nix"
with_nix_cargo_cache = true
```

This caches `/tmp/.cargo/registry`, `/tmp/.cargo/git`, and `target/`, keyed by
lockfiles, flake, Rust toolchain, Cargo config, runner architecture, and job
scope. Caching is opt-in because projects installing mutable Cargo tools into
`CARGO_HOME` may prefer the existing tool-cache behavior. It conflicts with
workflow-environment overrides of `CARGO_HOME` or `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.

These options apply to Rust language CI. The Cargo cache requires Actions; Crow
supports the generic `check_command` while retaining its dedicated
`[ci.crow].check_command` and secret policy, and exact-only Nix and Python
workflows use `[ci].components`. `[ci.crow].check_push_secret` passes a Crow
secret only to the push copy of `check_command` (pull requests run the same
gate without it). `[ci.crow].check_secret` supplies a secret to a single gate
on both `push` and `pull_request`—use it only for credentials that are already
read-only (such as a pull-only private cache token), allow `push` and
`pull_request` on the Crow secret, and list any other events like `manual` if
project-owned workflows need it too. The two keys are mutually exclusive.

## Cargo-Audit Reliability

Generated audit steps clone the advisory DB explicitly and run `cargo audit`
against the local database without fetching it again, avoiding repeated fetches
inside `cargo audit` and separating fetch failures from advisory failures:

```sh
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/RustSec/advisory-db.git "$db"
cargo audit --db "$db" --no-fetch --stale
```

## Runner Debugging

When Codeberg/Forgejo runners flake, separate stale from fresh runs:

1. Push or rerun on a new commit so the head SHA changes.
2. Poll only runs for that head.
3. Inspect exact run logs before editing code.

For Codeberg, check repository metadata first:

```sh
berg --owner-repo caniko/<repo> repo info
```

If local `berg` lacks Actions subcommands, poll the Codeberg API:

```sh
curl -fsSL "https://codeberg.org/api/v1/repos/caniko/<repo>/actions/runs?limit=10" |
  jq -r '.workflow_runs[] | [.id, (.html_url|split("/")[-1]), .status, .workflow_id] | @tsv'
```

`Input/output error (os error 5)` during rustc metadata writes indicates
runner/storage instability; `cargo package`, `cargo deny`, or test failures are
project or generator issues until reproduced otherwise.

## Fleet Adoption Checklist

For each repository:

1. Rebase the adoption branch onto the default branch.
2. Regenerate CI with the intended options.
3. Run `simit init ci ... --check --diff`.
4. Run locally the relevant package checks that failed in CI.
5. Push one repo-scoped branch.
6. Watch fresh Codeberg runs for that head only.
7. After merge, confirm at least one green default-branch CI run.

Fleet-level verification:

```sh
simit projects scan
simit projects list
```

Converted repos should leave `ci(hand-rolled)` for `ci(managed)` (generated
workflows only) or `ci(managed+extra)` (generated CI plus supplementary
non-generated workflows).
